_difficultyComment: There are no difficulty tiers. An Easy/Medium/Hard split existed twice — first as a control the player picked on Home, then as a badge on each campaign level — and both were removed on the owner's call. The campaign is one unbroken ramp and the level number is the whole of the difficulty: see _brainComment. A label covering three hundred levels told the player less than the number already on the tile, and it went stale the moment the curve moved. The opponent is called "Red Team" at every level, because the side is what it is and a rank name on a plate reads like a person.
_brainComment: The opponent climbs a straight line across the whole campaign: exponent 1.0 and rampLevels 1000 means every level is exactly 1/999 — 0.1% — stronger than the one before, level 1 at zero and level 1000 at full strength. Owner's call, and it replaces an eased curve (exponent 1.4) that finished at 601. The reason for the change: easing spent almost nothing early, leaving the brain only 8% up by level 100, so the first hundred levels were near-identical and the whole ladder leaned on card unlocks to feel different. A straight line moves 4.3 ms of reaction time and 0.001 of precision every level. Nobody feels one level of that — what a player feels is twenty levels of it, plus the two switches at 15 and 30.
_botCardComment: The bot's cards stay at level 1 for the first three hundred levels, so the opening third of the campaign is a fight against a brain that is improving and stats that are not — one thing changing at a time, while the player is still learning. From 301 the opponent's stats climb alongside its brain, and both reach maximum together at 1000: a perfect brain holding level 9 cards, which is +64% HP and damage. That is the finale, and it is meant to be a wall.
_unlockComment: Which campaign level hands over which card. The six in the starter deck are free from the start and are deliberately absent here. Everything else arrives on a curve that front-loads variety (a building, a swarm and a spell inside the first ten levels) and holds the expensive, swingy cards back. The last one lands at 110, just before the bot's own cards start levelling at 120 — so the full roster is in hand exactly when the opponent starts scaling. A card not named here is unlocked from the start.

levelNames._comment: A level name is built from one word of each list: first[(n-1) % 25] + second[(n-1) % 41]. The two lengths are coprime, so the pair does not repeat until level 1026 — every one of the 1000 levels gets its own name, and both halves change from one level to the next. Adding a word to either list is safe; making the two lengths share a factor is not, because the names would then start repeating early. The four arena names in levels.json (Primer Yard, Drip Works, Solvent Flats, Overspray Dome) deliberately use none of these words, so a level can never be mistaken for the board it is played on.
